about: Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith is a state university located in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, established on 10 February 1921 as Kashi Vidyapith and later renamed in honour of Mahatma Gandhi. According to its official website it is a public university administered under the state legislature of the government of Uttar Pradesh, with more than 350 affiliated colleges spread over five districts (Varanasi, Chandauli, Bhadohi, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra). It is described as one of the largest state universities in Uttar Pradesh. The university's official site lists faculties including Agriculture, Commerce & Management Studies, Education, Humanities, Law, Medical Sciences, Social Sciences, Social Work, and Science & Technology, and admits students through its Samarth-based admission portal for undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma and professional programmes.

identityNotes: Originally named Kashi Vidyapith, renamed Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith in 1995; founded during the non-cooperation movement and inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi. First VC was Dr. Bhagwan Das. Declared a State University in 1974 (earlier deemed university status).
